Iran International live blog, 26-27 November 2026

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi offered on Thursday to investigate jointly with Kuwait a drone strike that killed two Italian nationals, denying Iranian involvement in separate calls with his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts, Iran’s foreign ministry said.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called on Thursday for greater pressure on Iran to end its attacks on its Persian Gulf neighbors after an Iranian drone strike killed two Italian nationals in Kuwait.

Israel’s military is ready to strike Iran on its own, military spokesman Effie Defrin told Israeli public broadcaster Kan on Thursday.

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that China and Russia were providing little intelligence support to Iran, adding that both countries wanted the war to end and were helping him toward that goal.

Rear Admiral Habibollah Sayyari, deputy chief of the Iranian Army for Coordination, warned that the United States would face Iran’s newly developed air defense systems in the event of renewed military strikes, the semi-official Mehr news agency reported on Thursday.

Iran is rapidly constructing a fortified underground complex between two of its main nuclear sites that could house weapons systems or infrastructure linked to its nuclear program, a Washington-based research institute said on Wednesday.

A Nepali worker was killed and several others were injured after an aerial projectile struck Saudi Arabia’s Jazan oil refinery on Thursday amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, the Saudi Press Agency reported, citing an official source at the kingdom’s energy ministry.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guards’ aerospace force said on Friday that a US F-16 fighter jet had changed course after encountering warning fire from Iran’s air defenses southeast of Hengam Island in the Persian Gulf, state media reported.

The IRGC said the aircraft had approached Iranian airspace and was escorting and providing air cover for vessels it described as violating maritime regulations.

A senior Iranian army official said on Friday that the country’s armed forces, particularly its ground forces, were at their highest level of combat readiness, vowing to defend the country at any cost.

“We will resist any enemy, regardless of its capabilities, that sets its sights on our borders, for as long as we have blood in our veins,” said Sirous Amanollahi, deputy operations chief of the army’s ground forces.

Oman condemned attacks on Kuwait on Friday and renewed its call for an end to all military operations in the region, its foreign ministry said.

The ministry expressed solidarity with Kuwait, rejecting any infringement on its sovereignty, security and stability, and extended condolences to the families of the victims.

It also called for dialogue and diplomatic efforts to resolve disputes and preserve regional peace and security.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan formally approved a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on Friday, completing Ankara’s ratification of the pact, the Official Gazette said.

The agreement, signed in August amid the Iran war, stipulates that an attack on one party constitutes an attack on all.

Turkey’s parliament ratified the pact on November 5, paving the way for Ankara to provide military support to Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.

The US State Department said on Friday that Tehran had targeted nearly 2,000 Iranian citizens living abroad with fabricated charges.

In a post on its Persian-language X account, the department called Iran’s practice of freezing bank accounts and property belonging to relatives of critics abroad “a clear case of extortion.”

“Unable to silence their critics abroad, Tehran’s rulers are now using fabricated ‘espionage’ laws as a weapon to seize assets in Iran belonging to journalists, political activists and dissidents living abroad,” the post said.

The department said Iranian authorities were punishing retired parents in Iran for what their children said overseas. It also accused Tehran of misusing Interpol to seek unlawful extraditions.

“This regime continues to show its true nature. Freedom cannot be silenced through intimidation,” the department said.

Brent crude futures traded near their highest level this month in early Asian trading on Friday as continued attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure heightened concerns over oil supplies from the Middle East.

Brent crude fell 0.39% to $96.19 a barrel after gaining nearly $2 on Thursday to settle at its highest level since November 6. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 2.07% to $85.41 a barrel from Wednesday’s close, with no settlement on Thursday due to the Thanksgiving holiday, Reuters reported.

Both benchmarks were on track for their first weekly gain in four weeks.

An attack by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Aramco’s Jazan refinery on Thursday killed a Nepali worker, injured several others and temporarily halted some operations at the facility.

The attack came a day after the Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia’s largest oil refinery at Ras Tanura and the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan.

Given the supply disruptions caused by the Iran war, OPEC+ is likely to maintain its oil production targets for at least the first quarter of 2027 at a meeting on Sunday, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the talks.

South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun assured his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in a phone call on Thursday that Seoul had no intention of joining the war or deploying troops to the region, Iran’s embassy in Seoul said in a post on X.

Araghchi expressed concern over any foreign military presence in the region, saying it would escalate tensions and widen the conflict rather than contribute to peace and security.

The Iranian foreign minister also outlined recent diplomatic efforts and reiterated Tehran’s position on the conditions and framework for achieving regional peace.

South Korea plans to expand its anti-piracy naval mission to waters south of Oman, closer to the Strait of Hormuz, to protect its nationals and economic interests.

South Korean President Lee Jae-myung reaffirmed the plan on Wednesday but ruled out military operations in the Strait of Hormuz and its adjacent waters or involvement in the war with Iran.

Australia imposed counter-terrorism financing sanctions on two individuals accused of orchestrating antisemitic attacks in the country on behalf of the IRGC, Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong said in a statement on Thursday.

Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad are assessed to have used a network of proxies to orchestrate arson attacks targeting the Lewis Continental Kitchen in Sydney and the Adass Israel Synagogue in Melbourne in 2024, the statement said.

The activities of the two individuals were referenced in the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation’s (ASIO) annual threat assessment in June, but they have now been publicly named for the first time.

“These sanctions are an important step in disrupting the IRGC’s ability to conduct attacks against Australians and Australian interests,” Wong said.

The sanctions build on previous measures taken by Australia, including designating the IRGC as a state sponsor of terrorism, expelling Iran’s ambassador and three other diplomats, and suspending operations at its embassy in Tehran.

Under the sanctions, dealing with the assets of the two individuals or making assets available to them is a criminal offense. Violations of Australian sanctions laws carry penalties of up to 10 years in prison and/or heavy fines.

REUTERS/Hollie?Adams/File PhotoNov 27, 2026, 03:36 GMT+0Trump says China, Russia providing little support to IranUS President Donald Trump said on Thursday that China and Russia were providing little intelligence support to Iran and that both countries wanted to see the war end.

“I think that they’re very little involved with Iran. They could get involved, but involvement to me would mean shooting, not giving them little information,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida.

“We do the same thing, by the way. And you know, when they say that they may be spying on us, well, we spy on them too,” he added.

Asked about Russia’s intelligence sharing with Iran, Trump said, “I don’t think they give very much.”

Trump said the war with Iran had been discussed during his recent meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, adding that both leaders wanted the conflict to end.

“I think they’re helping me in that regard,” he said.
